He incites to the doing of sin, exploiting every opportunity to make man fall, and he was not content with that, but exploited even God's commandments to make propaganda for sin and make it known to people. Thus sin becomes something hateful and exceedingly sinful, because it was not ashamed of God's commandment but rather exploited it for its own benefit.

Perhaps you, my friend, have now realized that Satan wants to seduce you into sin even by exploiting the commandment itself. Therefore read and understand your Holy Bible well, going deeply into it with care, for how many people perished when they misunderstood some verses or interpreted them in a way that matched their personal desire, or adopted the principle of the single verse without trying to know the circumstances of the writing of each verse, how and to whom it was said, and without even comparing it with the rest of the texts of Scripture. And if you are a servant, or a father or a mother, do not speak in detail about sins lest you stir the senses of the one you serve, and do not speak about new kinds of sins lest you arouse the curiosity of the one you serve, so that he goes after these new sins to discover and practice them.

entries.section: (3) The conflict between the good will and the sin dwelling in

paragraphs.text: Here St. Paul begins, with wonderful eloquence, to describe the inner psychological conflict of the man who loves good but is overcome by evil, starting by declaring that he respects the Law and does not diminish its worth, since the Law is spiritual, delivered by the disposition of angels (Acts 7:53), and he casts all the causes of sin upon himself as a man of flesh and blood before his union with the Holy Spirit. So St. Paul says on behalf of every soul: I am a man "sold under sin" like a slave in the captivity of sin; the spiritual law demands that I follow goodness without help, and the result is that I am a man torn between the demands of the spirit and the reality of the flesh enslaved to sin.

entries.section: (3) The conflict between the good will and the sin dwelling in

paragraphs.text: I, as a man, do not understand this strange contradiction between my will and my conduct, for my will hates evil but I am overcome by it and weak before it, and the result is that I sin despite the cry of my conscience. For example, I want not to be angry, because anger causes many problems, but when I am provoked I fall into it. So I did not do what I want (longsuffering), but I did what I do not want, which is anger.

entries.section: (3) The conflict between the good will and the sin dwelling in

paragraphs.text: Since I do sin while in my inner self I do not want it, then I am at heart a friend of the Law; I love it and bear witness within me that it is good, because it rejects sin as I reject it.

entries.section: (3) The conflict between the good will and the sin dwelling in

paragraphs.text: Sin that dwells in me: the old man, that is, the nature inclined to evil that is within me. Who then does the sin, if I do not want to do it? It is the nature inclined to evil dwelling in me, that is, the old man.

entries.section: (3) The conflict between the good will and the sin dwelling in

paragraphs.text: Dwelleth in me: my nature inclined to evil.
I find not: I cannot do good because of my nature's inclination to evil.

The Apostle affirms the inclination of human nature to evil before the work of the grace of Christ in the New Testament, in the sacrament of Baptism and the rest of the sacraments. Although man's will, moved by conscience and the commandments of the Law, wants to do good, it cannot keep away from evil because of man's weak resistance to sin; rather, he inclines to it easily.

entries.section: (3) The conflict between the good will and the sin dwelling in

paragraphs.text: The final result is that I cannot do the good that my good will seeks, but I do evil because my nature is inclined to it. The good will is a mere desire that no power for carrying out supports, while all the inclinations of my nature go toward evil.

entries.section: (3) The conflict between the good will and the sin dwelling in

paragraphs.text: This is a confirmation of the previous verse, that the evil I do results from my nature inclined to it, against my good will, which is weak and unable to carry out the good.

entries.section: (3) The conflict between the good will and the sin dwelling in

paragraphs.text: Sadly, the increase of man's knowledge of goodness through the Law is matched, on the other hand, by an intensity of submission to evil, and in this he tears apart the human soul.

entries.section: (3) The conflict between the good will and the sin dwelling in

paragraphs.text: The inward man: the conscience of man, which moves his mind and heart to good, and is therefore in agreement with the good commandments of the Law.

entries.section: (3) The conflict between the good will and the sin dwelling in

paragraphs.text: There is another law, which is the law of sin, that is, my evil desires to carry out sin without limits, which compels me to commit sin although the law of my mind, that is, my conscience, rejects this sin.

entries.section: (3) The conflict between the good will and the sin dwelling in

paragraphs.text: Who will deliver me, the wretched man, after I have been unable to resist? My will is weak and powerless; it cannot give me victory over my body and my human thought, which wanted sin and did it, so that it became a body condemned to death. And the question received its answer: the Deliverer is Christ, by His saving grace through Baptism and the sacraments of the Church and all the means of grace.

entries.section: (3) The conflict between the good will and the sin dwelling in

paragraphs.text: St. Paul thanks God on my behalf and yours, since the Deliverer and Savior, our Lord Jesus Christ, has come to end the conflict and break the chains of sins, release the captives, and reconcile the inward man with the body, so that man is reconciled with God.

St. Paul also thanks God because the law of sin was in force over his body only and not over his mind, which served the law of God. In this his state was better than that of the Gentiles, who served the law of sin with the body and the mind also, so they walked in evil because the commandments of the Law did not warn them and they had only the conscience, which is easily warped and turned aside.

As for Paul, the problem of the law of sin dwelling in his body was solved when he received the sacrament of Baptism, so the old man died and he became, in mind and body, a servant of the laws and commandments of Christ. In this he received complete justification and became not liable to judgment, and the tears of repentance became a second baptism for him at any time he falls into sin, and then rises and declares his refusal to submit to it.

If you enjoy the grace of Christ which gives you strength to walk in the good way, do not give opportunity to the evil that dominates you, by keeping away from the sources of sin and drawing near to the Church, so that your strength increases. And do not be troubled by your many falls, for the grace of Christ to which you cling is able in the end to overcome every weakness or evil inclination that is generated within you as a result of your occasional negligence. Only persevere in repentance and in asking God's help.
The good pleasure of the loving Christ orders our life and gives us eternity

entries.section: (1) No condemnation to those who walk after the Spirit

paragraphs.text: Here we have reached with St. Paul the Holy of Holies of the Epistle, which is that those united with Christ Jesus have been rescued from judgment and the door of Paradise has finally been opened to them, on condition that they walk in a spiritual walk, subject to the commandments of Christ and not led after fleshly passions and desires.

entries.section: (1) No condemnation to those who walk after the Spirit

paragraphs.text: The law of the Spirit of life: the commandments of the New Testament supported by the power of the Holy Spirit.
The law of sin and death: the nature inclined to evil, which leads to man's destruction. Why is there no condemnation on the children of the New Testament?

Because the new spiritual law leading to eternal life has freed those united with Christ from the dominion of sin, that is, its law over them, and consequently freed them from death as the wages of sin. And how is that?
Through Christ, who was not content with commandments and teachings, but gave them the Holy Spirit, by whom they are able to carry out those commandments and overcome sin.

Note, beloved, that St. Paul mentioned the word Spirit in this chapter 20 times, in contrast to his mention of the word I, the defeated one, 20 times in the previous chapter, to highlight the helplessness of the I in contrast to victory by the Spirit in this chapter.

entries.section: (1) No condemnation to those who walk after the Spirit

paragraphs.text: It was weak: unable to support man in carrying out the commandment.
Weak through the flesh: the flesh weak before sin and inclined to it.
In the likeness of sinful flesh: Christ became incarnate in a complete human body but not inclined to sin, so he calls it "likeness" because it is pure and not inclined to sin.
For sin: to overcome sin and not fall into it.

Condemned sin: He showed its evil, for it had enslaved man throughout the Old Testament, but now, through the incarnation of Christ, man receives the new nature in the sacrament of Baptism, so he inclines to good and rejects evil. The Law showed goodness, but it was unable to help the flesh inclined to evil, so man was doing evil. But when Christ became incarnate to free us from sin, He gave us a new nature inclined to good, so He showed the error and evil of sin, and man no longer wants it as long as he is attached to God.

entries.section: (1) No condemnation to those who walk after the Spirit

paragraphs.text: In this we are able to fulfill the righteousness of the Law, so we are righteous in the Law's sight and it has nothing to complain of against us, because we have become walkers and led by the Spirit of God in a spiritual life. Note, beloved, that there is no contradiction between the commandments of the law of Moses and the commandments of Christ, as the Lord Christ Himself said, "Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil" (Mt 5:17).

entries.section: (1) No condemnation to those who walk after the Spirit

paragraphs.text: Those who are still under the dominion of the flesh, we find all their concerns and conversations confined to fleshly matters: what shall we eat, what shall we drink, what shall we wear, or what shall we enjoy? You find no place for spiritual matters in their lives. They are in the flesh and live for the flesh.

But the spiritual person who loves God and makes pleasing Him his first goal is concerned with spiritual things such as prayer, spiritual readings, fasts, and Liturgies, and you find his bodily concerns reasonable, balanced, and disciplined, that is, governed by the Spirit.

entries.section: (1) No condemnation to those who walk after the Spirit

paragraphs.text: The flesh is not evil in itself, but concern with and indulgence in fleshly desires is the error that leads to spiritual death and separation from God. As for the spiritual person, his heart is filled with peace, and his soul lives from the death of sin.

entries.section: (1) No condemnation to those who walk after the Spirit

paragraphs.text: What the flesh asks is opposed to what the Spirit asks, and the principle St. Paul lays down here is clear: whoever has focused all his concerns on his body has left God's sphere for the sphere of the world hostile to God, and cannot submit to the law of God even if he wants to, because his pampered body draws him to various desires, preventing him from carrying out the commandments pleasing to God. How can a slack body keep watch in prayer, how can a body stuffed with food fast, how can a swollen ego be humble, and how can the fornicator live a life of holiness?

entries.section: (1) No condemnation to those who walk after the Spirit

paragraphs.text: But if the Spirit of God dwells and lives in us, we are not called fleshly but spiritual, living in the world while it does not live in us, as though we were visitors, strangers to it, using from the world only what is necessary for our life with contentment and satisfaction, without greed or magnifying of living.

So all these preceding verses show that Baptism alone is not enough for our salvation unless we practice a life worthy of this gift after receiving it. And the one who has no love and conviction for the way of Christ, and is not submissive to the Holy Spirit, hindering His work, as though he did not have the Spirit of Christ within him, this one has no peace and will not have eternal life.

entries.section: (1) No condemnation to those who walk after the Spirit

paragraphs.text: If we walk by the Spirit and are united with Christ, then at the end of our life on earth the body will submit to natural death as a result of the original sin, while the spirit will have eternal life because of the life of righteousness we lived with the support of the Holy Spirit dwelling in us. Likewise, when Christ is united with us, the body dies to sin, that is, it rejects it and is repelled by it, while the spirit in which Christ works lives to righteousness by the grace of the Holy Spirit.

entries.section: (1) No condemnation to those who walk after the Spirit

paragraphs.text: The Spirit of Him that raised up Jesus: the Holy Spirit, who raised Christ: God the Father.
Shall also quicken your mortal bodies: although the body must die, it will rise on the last day in a new spiritual form, united with the spirit to be glorified with it.
His Spirit that dwelleth in you: the Holy Spirit.
So God is able to raise our bodies on the last day, that both the body and the spirit (the risen spiritual body) may enjoy the Kingdom of Heaven with Christ.
This verse also gives hope to every soul, that Christ is able to raise it from the falls of sin however hideous, if it wants repentance and insists on striving.

entries.section: (1) No condemnation to those who walk after the Spirit

paragraphs.text: After all the preceding free gifts of God, we are debtors to Him for our lives and our spirits, and it is not right for us to live as slaves of the flesh and its desires, as though we were debtors to the flesh for anything.

entries.section: (1) No condemnation to those who walk after the Spirit

paragraphs.text: For if we live doing the works of the flesh, which are evil desires (Gal 5:19, 20), the result is eternal death. But if we resist the works of the flesh by spiritual fullness, we can easily overcome, and then we enjoy eternal bliss with Christ.

entries.section: (1) No condemnation to those who walk after the Spirit

paragraphs.text: Are led: accept God's arrangements in their lives.

Here the Apostle shows the depth of the spiritual life with God. The person who confidently surrenders his life to God's leading, accepting from Him all the events of his life, thanking Him for the sweet ones and being patient in the bitter ones, this one is called a son of God.

entries.section: (1) No condemnation to those who walk after the Spirit

paragraphs.text: Abba: a Syriac word meaning father.
Father: an Arabic word meaning the Father.

Out of God's tenderness, He did not make our relationship with Him that of slaves fearing the punishment of their master, but a relationship of sonship to Him. He made us call Him with the boldness of sons, saying to Him "Abba" according to the language of the Jews, or Father according to the language of the Gentiles. That is, Paul affirms sonship in his repeated calling of God Father, as if he were saying: O Papa, Father.

entries.section: (1) No condemnation to those who walk after the Spirit

paragraphs.text: Heirs of God: since God is our Father, He gives us the eternal inheritance, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven.

Joint-heirs with Christ: Christ is the firstborn among many brethren. He entered the Kingdom as our representative, so that we also may enter on the last day and enjoy with Him His gifts in the Kingdom. We do not say "our Father" with the mouth only, but the Spirit of God within us assures us of this feeling that we are truly His beloved children, and therefore heirs of the Kingdom with His Son Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son. And if God allows us sufferings on earth, it is because He loves those who strive and endure; the Lord Christ walked first the way of sufferings and then glory, and so we also suffer first and then are glorified with an eternal glory.

God gives you, my brother, the grace of sonship and the inheritance of eternal life if you live spiritually, so how can you give up your great position and be occupied with the passing desires of the flesh?! By your spiritual conduct you are higher than the rest of the creatures, so how do you descend to animal conduct?... Let your delight be to be with God, and lift your eyes toward eternity, your natural place, and if you fall into a vile desire rise quickly, and the Holy Spirit will help you to live as a son of God.

entries.section: (2) The renewal of creation and the hope of the coming glory

paragraphs.text: Who can put the limited sufferings of the present time in comparison with the glory to come that is about to be revealed in us and which we shall receive in endless eternity? The endurance of the sufferings of this age has an unlimited reward of eternal joy and happiness, and for this reason the saints longed for sufferings in order to increase their account in the coming eternal glory.

entries.section: (2) The renewal of creation and the hope of the coming glory

paragraphs.text: The creature: all creatures other than man, which were created for him, and were cursed because of his sin, and will be changed in eternity when man is glorified.
Eternity, in which our return to the divine embrace is completed so that we may enjoy the fullness of sonship to God, is the object of the expectation of the whole creation.

entries.section: (2) The renewal of creation and the hope of the coming glory

paragraphs.text: The creature was made subject to vanity, that is, the curse came upon it when Adam sinned, "cursed is the ground for thy sake" (Gen 3:17), and the phrase "not willingly" means not as a result of a fault arising from nature, but as a command of God who subjected it to destruction, yet it has a hope of being renewed and freed from the corruption and curse that came upon it, just as the children of God will be freed. But it will not be glorified, because glory belongs only to rational beings, but it will be changed to become spiritual and not material when the new heaven and the new earth appear (Rev 21:1), in which man lives forever in the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.section: (2) The renewal of creation and the hope of the coming glory

paragraphs.text: Creation still groans in pain to this day, since it is still a stage for wars, massacres, and famines because of man's evil, and it still travails (as if it were a womb in pain at the delivery of the child) with earthquakes, volcanoes, floods, and fires, waiting for when these painful events will end, and then nature will come to a better state suited to the revealing of man as a son of God in eternity, that is, it will be transformed, as we said, into a new heaven and a new earth.

entries.section: (2) The renewal of creation and the hope of the coming glory

paragraphs.text: The firstfruits of the Spirit: we have tasted the pledge of eternity in fellowship with God as a preparation for the complete fellowship in heaven.
Groan within ourselves: the sufferings that the children of God endure on earth.
Adoption: the complete sonship to God that we receive in eternity.
The redemption of our body: when bodies are changed from the material nature and dust to spiritual bodies, this we receive as grace from Christ who redeemed our spirits and our bodies.

If St. Paul, in an eloquent figure, pictured nature to us as a person who feels and senses, how much more do we human beings groan, although we have tasted some blessings of the Holy Spirit in part as a pledge of the age to come, yet we long for the whole and not the part. The fullness of sonship is not completed except after the resurrection of the bodies from death, which Christ redeemed.

entries.section: (2) The renewal of creation and the hope of the coming glory

paragraphs.text: The phrase "we are saved by hope" does not mean that we have already received salvation, but means that we are certain that God will fulfill for us His promise of salvation in eternal life, because God's promises are sure since He is truthful. Salvation, resurrection, and the fullness of sonship are eschatological states that take their true, open existence only in the age to come, while what we enjoy now is only a pledge of the invisible age to come. For this reason God gave us hope, by which we are confident that we shall receive eternal life, which is not seen now. Hope, beloved, is like a check in your hands now, but the date of cashing it and benefiting from it is after you leave the body, and your only weapon in cashing it is to preserve it from being lost, and to be patient until the date of cashing it at the end of your life.

If the sufferings of life are temporary, do not be troubled by them however much they multiply, but you can rise above them if you look at the heavenly glory that awaits you, and then you will receive divine help and have compassion on those who wrong you and pray for them. And although you see the sufferings with your eyes, you hardly feel them because of the abundance of God's grace supporting you.

entries.section: (3) The intercession of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: How are we to be patient amid the sufferings of the present and a salvation that is unseen, for the obtaining of which we pray yet do not understand its nature? In this we do not know what we should pray for, that is, the Kingdom, so the Holy Spirit intervenes to support us in our striving, give us His graces, and help us in our weakness, and not only that, but He intercedes for us and teaches us how to pray, that is, He inspires man with a prayer of the heart that the human tongue is unable to express, and gives our hearts depth in understanding and perceiving the mysteries of God that the human mind is unable to perceive. And we, as weak human beings, how do we stand before the great, holy God and speak with Him? Here the Holy Spirit intervenes and gives us the feelings with which we approach God and teaches us how to speak with Him.

entries.section: (3) The intercession of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: The saints: God's children sanctified in Him, for everyone who believes is sanctified and set apart for Christ. The Spirit searches, that is, perceives the heart of each person individually, giving him what suits his level. The most important thing to the Spirit is the completeness of man's salvation, so He purifies our prayers of requests harmful to our salvation and answers only the requests that are according to the will of God, which certainly bring good to us.

If you do not know what to say in prayer, or the devil wars against you with laziness or wandering of thought or boredom, do not be troubled, but stand to pray and ask God's help, and He will support you and teach you everything. And what you do with difficulty now will become easy and a comfort to your heart; indeed, you will long for prayer and not want to end it, and all this by the work of the Holy Spirit dwelling in you.

entries.section: (4) Christ the Orderer and Intercessor

paragraphs.text: God's plan for us is surpassing, for He turns all things without exception to the edification of the believer's soul, so that they work for his good on earth or for his glory in heaven. The phrase "work together" means that some individual events in our lives seem bad, harsh, and incomprehensible, but when they are added to other events, they work together in harmony, and the final picture is completed for the good and benefit of man. What seems harm now carries within it good in the future. But this privilege is only for those who love God, who, after God called them, responded to Him with love, obedience, and surrender, and lived their lives fulfilling God's purpose, that is, His will in their lives.

Note, beloved, that God's call alone does not bring about salvation, but rather the intention of those called and their obedience to God after the call. The call is not binding or compulsory, as the Lord Christ said, "For many be called, but few chosen" (Mt 20:16). So if God encourages you to a prayer, a reading, or any service, do not be lazy or put up obstacles, but hasten to respond so that you become a true son to Him.

entries.section: (4) Christ the Orderer and Intercessor

paragraphs.text: The firstborn among many brethren: Christ, after His resurrection, ascended to heaven to declare the possibility of man's entering into the glories in the Kingdom. He is the firstborn of all who believe in Him, whom He considers brethren, that is, they will share the glory with Him in the Kingdom after they complete their spiritual striving in this life.

Whom he called: this confirms that every person who has the readiness to believe, God will call and he will receive eternal salvation. There will be no person to whom the call to life with God and to faith did not reach, except those who have no readiness for life with God, whom God knows by His foreknowledge.

God's purpose is that man should be loved as a son to Him, so He gives him a glory like the glory of His Son Jesus Christ the Firstborn. God's choosing of some and appointing them as sons to Him is not done on the basis of partiality, but on the basis of His foreknowledge of them ("whom he did foreknow") that they would respond to His call, and those who respond to the call God has justified by Baptism. So those who are steadfast in love and striving have in the end the eternal heavenly glory prepared for them before the foundation of the world.

entries.section: (4) Christ the Orderer and Intercessor

paragraphs.text: If God is with us, that is, supports us and helps us in our weakness, then which of the wicked, or opposing factors, or adverse forces can drive us out of the circle of God's love as long as we hold fast to Him?

entries.section: (4) Christ the Orderer and Intercessor

paragraphs.text: We cannot doubt God's love, since for our sake He gave the dearest thing He had, His only Son Jesus Christ. So it is obvious that He will give us all the gifts and graces necessary for our salvation.

entries.section: (4) Christ the Orderer and Intercessor

paragraphs.text: If Satan accuses us of our sins before God every day, behold, Christ justifies us through our repentance.

entries.section: (4) Christ the Orderer and Intercessor

paragraphs.text: If the wicked liars condemn us in the world with slander, as they condemned the martyrs and saints, what is the value of their condemnation when the true judgment has been placed in the hand of Christ, who died and rose and sat at the right hand of the Father, interceding for us with His blood an atoning intercession that delivers us from judgment.

entries.section: (5) Nothing separates us from our love for Christ

paragraphs.text: Since God's love for us is infinite and beyond doubt, Satan's attempts are directed toward us with exhausting trials and tribulations, and their aim is to prevent us from loving God, and Satan often succeeds in that. But St. Paul cries out with confidence together with the elect who are steadfast in their love for God, saying that nothing separates us from God, whether tribulation, which is pressure and injustice, or distress, which is more violent than tribulation, persecution, that is, inflicting harm and crushing, and famine, which is the cutting off of all the resources of life, and nakedness, that is, lack of necessary clothing, then peril and sword, that is, the threat to the Christian's life even unto death.

entries.section: (5) Nothing separates us from our love for Christ

paragraphs.text: History bears witness to the multitude of martyrs who are killed all the day long, that is, throughout the days, like sheep, because of their love for the King Christ. And every Christian accepts death throughout his life in enduring sufferings, whether in the struggle against sin, or asceticism, or self-giving service, and even more in the torments of martyrdom for the love of Christ.

entries.section: (5) Nothing separates us from our love for Christ

paragraphs.text: Thus we win a great victory over Satan and his helpers, and enter into eternal glory, after Satan has exhausted all his tricks of tribulations and death in the hope of turning us away from our love for Christ; indeed, we are more than conquerors through the very things that were set for our snares, and if we are struck we are counted stronger than those who strike, because God wrestles with us.

entries.section: (5) Nothing separates us from our love for Christ

paragraphs.text: St. Paul returns to affirm that our love for Christ, who loved us first, cannot be weakened by fear of death or love of life. As for his mention of the angels and some of their orders (principalities and powers), what is meant is that we love Christ not for the sake of our future enjoyment of the presence of the angels, but for the sake of His beloved Person.
The Paradise of the Fathers tells us that a monk saw a real angel while he was praying, and he continued in his prayer without paying attention to the angel.

Nor can the enticements of the world in the present and the future, which rise and fall in many fluctuations, or any other creature, whatever it may be, separate us from our love for Christ; the goal of our life is to love Him and to enjoy His love for us, and welcome to death if it shortens our way to meet our heavenly Bridegroom.
Examine yourself at the end of each day: what hindered you from enjoying the love of Christ, and however dear it is, do not let it deprive you of the goal of your life.
Make more room of time and give up, not only evil desires or the worries and disturbances of life, but any occupation that deprives you of your spiritual life.
Election and faith

entries.section: (1) Paul's sorrow over the unbelief of the Jews

paragraphs.text: In this chapter St. Paul declares the extent of his love and zeal for the salvation of the Jews who did not believe, saying, with all the sincerity flowing from his union with Christ, and with the witness of both his conscience and the Holy Spirit, that he does not lie when he says that he is very sorrowful from the depths of his heart because of the unbelief of many of the Jews in Christ.

entries.section: (1) Paul's sorrow over the unbelief of the Jews

paragraphs.text: Paul wishes the salvation of the Jews even if it were at the cost of himself, as Moses did long ago in his intercession for the children of Israel when they sinned, and Moses said to God, "Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written" (Ex 32:32). The words of St. Paul should not be taken literally, for he certainly does not wish to be cut off from Christ, of whom he said in the previous chapter, "Who shall separate us from the love of Christ?" Rather, he said these words to clear himself of the charge that he had sacrificed them and disowned them as his people, his kinsmen, and his relatives according to the flesh after his faith in Christ; indeed, he shows his self-giving love toward them because he was moved by the love of Christ the Redeemer on the Cross.

entries.section: (1) Paul's sorrow over the unbelief of the Jews

paragraphs.text: Paul does not forget the great privileges with which God singled them out above all other peoples, for they are:

Israelites: the title Jacob received from God so that his offspring might become a people special to Him. To them pertaineth the adoption: "Ye are the children of the Lord your God" (Deut 14:1). And the glory: the only people in the world who saw the glory of God in the form of the pillars of cloud and fire in the wilderness and in the tabernacle.
The covenants: how many covenants of love God made with them, yet, what a wonder, they turned back from their covenants with God.
The giving of the law: the Law that revealed God's will and disciplined man.
The service of God: He taught them how to worship God with prayer, rites, and the offering of sacrifices. The promises: those connected with the coming of the Messiah, the Savior of the world.

entries.section: (1) Paul's sorrow over the unbelief of the Jews

paragraphs.text: The fathers: they are Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, beloved of God.

And more important than all that precedes is the coming of the Lord Christ from their offspring, from the flesh of the Virgin Mary, yet He is not an ordinary man but an eternal, everlasting God, to whom be all glory and blessing forever, Amen.

If God has granted you circumstances that help you in the spiritual life, make use of them and enjoy your sonship to God, lest if you neglect them they condemn you on the last day. Seize every opportunity and respond to the voice of God today in order to draw near to Him.

entries.section: (2) God's promise to the elect only

paragraphs.text: Perhaps some think that the word of God has failed, that is, God's promise of the salvation of the people of Israel.

So Paul denied that, affirming that the word of God and His promises are firm and do not fail through the ages. For God's promise is only for the true, spiritual Israelite who will be joined to Christ the promised Savior, who is the goal of the Old Testament, and not for all the children of Abraham according to the flesh, as proved by the fact that Ishmael is a son of Abraham according to the flesh but did not receive the promise; rather the promise is fulfilled through Isaac, who would keep the faith firm like his father until Christ came, who is the goal of the promise and the blessing to Abraham.

entries.section: (2) God's promise to the elect only

paragraphs.text: Sonship is fundamentally sonship to God, and the condition of sonship to God is not sonship to Abraham according to the flesh, but faith and holding fast to God's promises, that is, faith in Christ.

entries.section: (2) God's promise to the elect only

paragraphs.text: When He promised Sarah that she would have a son in her old age, Sarah became a vessel for raising up the offspring of God.

entries.section: (2) God's promise to the elect only

paragraphs.text: To affirm that God's choice is not limited to fleshly descent, St. Paul gave a strong example in Jacob and Esau, the twins from the womb of Rebecca, the wife of our father Isaac, who were alike in father and mother.

entries.section: (2) God's promise to the elect only

paragraphs.text: Here God did not choose both, but by His foreknowledge looked at the future of each of them and found Jacob, the younger, more loving toward Him and more careful to please Him than his brother, so God chose him although Jacob's works were not perfect, for he fell into the sins of deceit and lying. And the phrase (not of works) means that however much a person's works attain of righteousness, he has not yet reached the degree of deserving God's choice of him, but the choice is a gift and an overflowing grace from God who loves mankind who respond to Him, to support them and raise them to His perfection.

entries.section: (2) God's promise to the elect only

paragraphs.text: Although Esau was the elder, God chose Jacob, and he became lord over Esau, because he was better qualified to inherit the virtues and blessing of Isaac his father.

entries.section: (2) God's promise to the elect only

paragraphs.text: So God's love for Jacob came not as partiality from God toward him, but because He had foreseen him to be worthy of this love. Jacob's good works came afterward, confirming the exactness of God's choice of him, and as a simple offering from Jacob to the loving God, while God's hatred of Esau was not an injustice to him but based on God's foreknowledge that Esau was a hard-hearted man who made light of grace.

And also, not everyone in the Church is elect, for the Church, like Rebecca, bears the chosen person and the rejected person. So be careful, beloved, to be among the elect who please God's heart by your obedience to His commandments.

entries.section: (3) God's choice and man's freedom

paragraphs.text: Certainly God is not unjust, and God's choosing of one person and not another never means that God has determined eternal bliss for some and eternal destruction for others, otherwise man would not be responsible for his life; but the truth is that God's choice is based on His foreknowledge of man's heart, conduct, works, and all the details of his life.
So the conclusion is that God chooses the person who wants to choose God.

entries.section: (3) God's choice and man's freedom

paragraphs.text: Therefore God said to Moses: with all my esteem for man in his striving and his works, this does not mean that the heavenly gifts man receives are the price of this striving, but they are an invaluable grace granted certainly to those who strive and withheld from the slack. Therefore God said, "I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion," because all the credit in grace goes back to my mercy and compassion, and consequently it is not Israel's right to be angry because of my choosing the Gentiles, for my mercy and compassion, based on my foreknowledge, belong to me alone as God.

entries.section: (3) God's choice and man's freedom

paragraphs.text: "Not of him that willeth": does not mean that God gives no weight to the human will and human striving by good works, but its meaning is that man by his will and striving is unable to reach a good enough level to deserve compassion and mercy, and that the doing of good is among the mercies of God's grace supporting human helplessness, as the Lord Christ said, "without me ye can do nothing" (Jn 15:5). Therefore the result came: not of him that willeth, but of God that sheweth mercy.
Do not persist in an evil in your heart, however many good works you have, for they will not profit you. You must purify your heart by repentance and forgiveness so that you may be saved.

entries.section: (3) God's choice and man's freedom

paragraphs.text: When God wanted to deliver His people Israel from the land of Egypt, He chose Pharaoh, hard-hearted and resisting God, to show God's longsuffering in bearing Pharaoh's delay and stubbornness throughout the period of the ten plagues. And He chose Moses, the meek, and raised and glorified him, to deliver the people from the hand of Pharaoh. The phrase "whom he will he hardeneth" means that God allowed Pharaoh to show the hardness that was already in him and to defy God, but if God had willed, He would have destroyed Pharaoh from the first plague, yet He left him in his hardness time after time so that God might be glorified in the end.

entries.section: (3) God's choice and man's freedom

paragraphs.text: Some misunderstood the preceding verse and thought that God toys with human hearts, putting mercy in some and hardness in others against their will, and consequently He has no right to blame anyone, as though man were driven and not free to choose.

entries.section: (3) God's choice and man's freedom

paragraphs.text: Here St. Paul returns to speaking to the Jews, who denied God's right to bring the Gentiles into the fold of faith. St. Paul replies to them sharply, "Who art thou, O Jew, that repliest against God?" God's will, His desire, and His mercy are matters that belong to Him alone and are at the very heart of His work as God, who has all power, depth of thought, and perfection of justice in His choices, and no person has the right to call God to account, because the creature has no right to judge the Creator, since his understanding counts as nothing before God's unlimited wisdom.

You have the right to speak with God with all that is in your heart with the innocence of a child, and be confident that He loves you and wants to hear your voice. Only humble yourself before Him and speak as you wish even if you express yourself wrongly, for He will guide you because He is your tender Father.

entries.section: (3) God's choice and man's freedom

paragraphs.text: Paul cited the parable of the potter who has absolute authority over one lump of clay to make of it a vessel unto honor, like a beautiful work of art, or a vessel unto dishonor, like a flowerpot.

entries.section: (3) God's choice and man's freedom

paragraphs.text: The vessels of wrath is Pharaoh, hard-hearted from the beginning, perishing in all cases; God used him as a visual aid to show His wrath against the wicked and the power of His vengeance on them, by drowning Pharaoh and the Egyptians in the Red Sea, after He had endured him throughout the period of the ten plagues. We note that St. Paul did not say that God is the one who made the vessels of wrath, but only that He endured them, because man by his own evil becomes a vessel that angers God.

entries.section: (3) God's choice and man's freedom

paragraphs.text: The vessels of mercy is Israel, humiliated from slavery in the land of Egypt, whom He took to the Promised Land, and they became a people of consequence, and He made for them a great name, glorified among the peoples, and here the greatness of God's mercy toward them appeared. And so God does with many who appear persecuted and humiliated in the world for His name's sake, but He supports them and then glorifies them in heaven.

entries.section: (3) God's choice and man's freedom

paragraphs.text: As God chose the wretched Jews to have mercy on them, so also His mercy extended to include the wretched Gentiles, to make of them His people, that is, the Church of the New Testament, side by side with Christians of Jewish origin.

entries.section: (3) God's choice and man's freedom

paragraphs.text: The matter of God's choosing the Gentiles is not a new matter to the Jews, because many prophecies of the Old Testament spoke about the entrance of the Gentiles into the Church, such as Hosea (2:23), who said that the Gentiles who were not of the people of God became His people, and those who were hated became beloved.

entries.section: (3) God's choice and man's freedom

paragraphs.text: The peoples and places that previously refused to worship God have become children of God.

The Church teaches us never to judge anyone as lost, however sinful, until he dies. For today's sinner may be tomorrow's saint, and the reverse is true. Nor do we hasten to declare a person's holiness except after his repose and the Church's assurance of the truthfulness of his life. So offer prayers for every person who sins, and show him your love more than to the righteous believers.

entries.section: (3) God's choice and man's freedom

paragraphs.text: As for Israel, the people numerous as the sand of the sea, they rejected Christ, but at the end of days some of the Jews will believe in the Lord Christ and be saved (Isa 10:22).

entries.section: (3) God's choice and man's freedom

paragraphs.text: Finishing the work: God will prolong His longsuffering until He accomplishes His purpose and His love in the salvation of some of the Jews at the end of days.

Cutting it short in righteousness: God is like any just ruler who will judge in righteousness the Jews who will believe at the end of days. Left us a seed: the remnant who will believe from among the Jews at the end of days.

God will continue to call the Jews to faith until the end of days, and a number whom He calls a little seed will believe in Him, and for the sake of these He is longsuffering toward the people of Israel to this day, and has not destroyed them like the people of Sodom and Gomorrah (Isa 1:9). This declares that there is a number of Jews who will believe in Christ although many of them have refused faith.

Do you not notice with me, beloved, the longsuffering and compassion of God? He is the one who endured Pharaoh many times, and was patient with the people of Israel for about 2000 years, and so He is patient with us to give us every opportunity for repentance, so that even if we are hard-hearted we may be ashamed before His love and hasten to Him in repentance.

entries.section: (4) The reason for the Gentiles' justification and the Jews' stumbling

paragraphs.text: The Gentiles, who lived in the darkness of spiritual ignorance and did not walk in the way of the works of the Law, have now arrived at justification by faith; while the people of Israel, who spent their whole lives seeking to carry out the Law in every letter, did not perceive the depth of the law of righteousness and that it leads to reaching Christ, and the result was that they did not obtain true righteousness.

entries.section: (4) The reason for the Gentiles' justification and the Jews' stumbling

paragraphs.text: St. Paul gives the reason why Israel did not attain righteousness, which is that it did not seek righteousness by faith in Christ, but sought it as a price it deserved as a natural result of its walking by the works of the Law, so the Israelites stumbled at a stone, who is the Lord Christ, who exposed their hypocrisy and rejected their self-righteousness and pride, and so all they did was to crucify Him and kill Him and deny His resurrection.

entries.section: (4) The reason for the Gentiles' justification and the Jews' stumbling

paragraphs.text: St. Paul cited the book of Isaiah (Isa 8:14) in support of his words, that the Jews who rejected Christ stumbled at Him, so they fell and went out from the fold of faith. But whoever trusts in the Lord Christ, the Rock of ages, the cornerstone, and the foundation of the Church, shall not be ashamed and will not be exposed to eternal shame in the judgment.

Therefore let us bow down in thanksgiving to our God, who came to us with His righteousness, and counted us as vessels of mercy, chose us and had compassion on us, and made us vessels unto honor and glory according to His will. But we, beloved, must remain firm in this choice, or we too will be rejected, as Israel was rejected because of the hardness of its heart.

And all this does not nullify or abolish the place and importance of the Law in the Old Testament; rather the Law, like a great commander, now retires and hands over the command to the new Commander, our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom be all glory and honor. The Jews' rejection of faith and the Gentiles' acceptance of it

entries.section: (1) The Jews seek their own righteousness

paragraphs.text: St. Paul declares that the desire of his heart, his delight, and his prayers are for the salvation of Israel, for his heart is torn with pain, sorrow, and grief over the children of Israel who rejected Christ and so were rejected by God.

entries.section: (1) The Jews seek their own righteousness

paragraphs.text: Here is St. Paul, with an eye of pure love that does not criticize, looking at the one sweet advantage in the Jews, which is their intense holding to God and their zeal for His name, though it lacks spiritual knowledge, remembering himself personally when he was very zealous for God; in his ignorance he persecuted the Christians before his heart was enlightened by the vision of Christ.

entries.section: (1) The Jews seek their own righteousness

paragraphs.text: The righteousness of God: the work of the merciful God in the believer's life to justify him, as a gift to submissive, humble believers.

The Jews in their pride ignored the righteousness of Christ and wanted to prove their worthiness by justifying themselves by their works, to take all the glory and praise for their swollen selves, and the result was that they did not obtain righteousness because of their pride.

entries.section: (1) The Jews seek their own righteousness

paragraphs.text: The Jews were ignorant that the whole aim of the Law, the sacrifices, and the Old Testament is to prepare mankind to receive Christ, who gives righteousness to everyone who believes in Him.

entries.section: (1) The Jews seek their own righteousness

paragraphs.text: St. Paul returns to convince the Jews of the impossibility of justification by the Law, because Moses laid down a condition, which is that man do all the works of the Law and not err in a single one of them in order to receive justification and so live. But who of mankind can do that?!

Would that you looked at people's virtues and not at their faults to condemn them. And know that no person, however wicked, can be without virtues. If you train your eyes to discover people's virtues, that is, to praise them, you will give rest to your heart and benefit from these virtues, and at the same time win the love of others, and then you will look at their faults with an eye of compassion and find excuses for them and pray for them.

entries.section: (2) The righteousness of Christ is available to every person

paragraphs.text: "Who shall ascend into heaven?": So people asked in the Old Testament, since they saw righteousness high and far from them like heaven, and they said: is there a person who can rise to heaven and live righteousness?! That is, there is not one righteous person who can fulfill the Law.
"To bring Christ down": People wished for and awaited the Messiah the Savior and said in the Old Testament: who will rise to heaven to bring us the Christ who gives us righteousness?

Justification by faith has now become possible, after the spiritual life had been as far from man as heaven is from earth, but the Lord Christ by His Incarnation brought the spiritual world and the heavenly things down to us on earth, into our hearts and our Church.

entries.section: (2) The righteousness of Christ is available to every person

paragraphs.text: Christ offered us redemption on a silver platter, when He died and then went down to Hades to free the captives in it, and then rose from the dead without any effort from you and without anyone asking you to go down to Hades to raise Him. This is in comparison with the exhausting efforts required of the believer in the Old Testament, of offering sacrifices..... and so on.
And all you have to do is to believe in His resurrection and in the power of His justification, and not be like the Jews who denied His resurrection, saying, "Who can bring Christ up from Hades?"

For the Jews were unable to understand the work of the Messiah, how He would come up from the Hades to which He went down, to bring up those who died in hope, and they forgot that He is God, able to raise Himself and to raise with Him all who died in hope.

Yes, beloved, salvation has become within reach through Christ Jesus. Shall we not make use of this opportunity while we are alive on earth, lest the time pass us by? That is by repentance and partaking of the Holy Mysteries, which results in being concerned with speaking with God in prayer and reading His word in the Holy Bible every day.

entries.section: (2) The righteousness of Christ is available to every person

paragraphs.text: By our confession of Christ, but not an oral confession. The Christian of old used to confess Christ with the sword at his neck, but let us confess Christ at least:
a- By our good conduct and our outward behavior, so that we bear witness that we are children of God.
b- By our faith of the heart that the God who raised Christ from the dead is able to raise us from all our falls, so that our inner life is purified and thus we are saved.

entries.section: (2) The righteousness of Christ is available to every person

paragraphs.text: So the person who is sanctified by his conduct and his heart receives righteousness and salvation.

entries.section: (2) The righteousness of Christ is available to every person

paragraphs.text: All who believed receive victory over their sins and glory and honor in eternity.

entries.section: (2) The righteousness of Christ is available to every person

paragraphs.text: Since the Jew and the Greek (the Gentile) are equal in their sins before God, so everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord, whether Jew or Greek, is equal in receiving righteousness from the one God, rich in His generosity and giving to mankind.

entries.section: (2) The righteousness of Christ is available to every person

paragraphs.text: For everyone who makes Christ his God (calls upon the name of the Lord) by faith will be saved, and why? Because he has become one with Christ, and has the resurrection and life of Christ, who is the only way to salvation. Of course this does not mean that salvation is by mere general faith in God - that is, as in any religion, as the Catholic Church claims in the heresy of "the universality of salvation" - but salvation has conditions set by the Holy Bible.

How great is the generosity of our Lord Jesus Christ, who does not look at faces but at the heart. The world divides people into positions and ranks, rich and poor. A mother may discriminate among her children by partiality, but in Christ Jesus all people have equal opportunities to obtain salvation. So do not be distressed by your weaknesses and shortcomings, for Christ loves you and is ready to supply all your needs and give you complete joy.

entries.section: (3) The Jews' rejection of the preaching

paragraphs.text: For any person to call on the name of the Lord, that is, to pray to Christ and consider Him God, he must first believe in Him, and that is after he hears about Him through a preacher (evangelist).

entries.section: (3) The Jews' rejection of the preaching

paragraphs.text: For the preachers to succeed in their mission, they must be sent from God in the name of the Lord Christ by the grace and help of the Holy Spirit. Isaiah (Isa 52:7) had earlier blessed their weary feet and described them as bringing glad tidings of peace, good things, salvation, and freedom from sin. They are not like the prophets of the Old Testament who carried threats and warnings, while the glad tidings were postponed until Christ came.
We ask ourselves as servants: does peace show in our lives so that everyone is drawn to our Christ who gives peace, or do the worries and desires of the world appear in us?!

entries.section: (3) The Jews' rejection of the preaching

paragraphs.text: It was supposed that the Jews would be the first to believe the news, and even to take part themselves in preaching Christ like the rest of the apostles, but instead they did not believe the good news of the Gospel but resisted it, and Isaiah had earlier prophesied about them (Isa 53:1), saying, "Who hath believed our report?" from Israel, that is, the preaching of Christ.

entries.section: (3) The Jews' rejection of the preaching

paragraphs.text: Faith is accomplished by believing the report and the Incarnation and redemption of Christ, who is the Word of God, and therefore whoever rejects the report rejects God Himself.

entries.section: (3) The Jews' rejection of the preaching

paragraphs.text: The Israelites are responsible for their rejection, and they have no argument that they did not hear the report, because the preaching of Christ reached all the regions of the inhabited world through the apostles, and also through the Jews gathered on the day of Pentecost from all the countries of the world. These, when they learned the news of the resurrection of Christ, believed, and then each went off to his country to carry the glad tidings to his Jewish relatives scattered throughout the world.

entries.section: (3) The Jews' rejection of the preaching

paragraphs.text: Certainly Israel knew the news of the Gospel and rejected it by their own will. Here St. Paul cites two great prophets, Moses and Isaiah, who prophesied about Israel's rejection of faith in Christ. First, Moses prophesied in Deuteronomy (32:21) that God would reject them as His people and provoke them to jealousy by accepting the Gentiles, whom He called of old "a foolish nation" in regard to spiritual matters. And if the Gentiles understood God's wisdom, what excuse have the Jews for not understanding, they who are the intelligent?
Second, God spoke through Isaiah (65:1), saying: I, as God, have become understood and clear to those who did not seek me or ask about me, that is, the Gentiles.

Here a person outside the Church may hear about Christ, and his heart is filled with love for Him, and he offers strong repentance and a new holy life more than an outwardly religious and inwardly proud person. So do not rely on your habit of attachment to the Church, but let there be inward repentance in you and an effort to understand what you pray and hear.

entries.section: (3) The Jews' rejection of the preaching

paragraphs.text: But as for Israel, "All day long I have stretched forth my hands," I, God, in love to them (throughout the period of the Old Testament) through the calling of the prophets. But as for them, their hearts turned to stone and they resisted me and were stubborn toward me. The phrase "stretched forth my hands" is a reference to the Cross of Christ, where He was stretching out (opening) His arms to mankind, stubborn and refusing His salvation, that perhaps it might repent.
The faith of the Jews before the end of days

entries.section: (1) The future of the Jews with regard to salvation

paragraphs.text: Although God described Israel as a stubborn people in the previous chapter, this does not mean at all that He closed the door of salvation to those among them who want to believe in Him. The proof is that St. Paul himself, an Israelite of the tribe of Benjamin, was accepted by God when he responded to the love of Christ for him, and He brought him into the fold of faith, not only as a believer but as a great preacher.

entries.section: (1) The future of the Jews with regard to salvation

paragraphs.text: God, who chose Israel as His people, cannot reject them, even after they crucified Him and rejected Him. Although He rejected them as a political state when He said, "Behold, your house is left unto you desolate" (Mt 23:38), announcing the end of the Jewish religion, He will remain always and forever with open arms toward everyone from the people of Israel who believes in Him. For in every generation there is a small Israelite remnant who believe in Him. The proof is that when the prophet Elijah complained to God about the people of Israel, saying that they had killed the prophets and torn down the altars (that is, they had replaced the worship of God with the worship of idols), and that they sought to kill Elijah himself, God answered that He had seven thousand men who had not bowed the knee to Baal (1 Kgs 19:18). The number seven signifies perfection and the number one thousand heavenly life, that is, the seven thousand live in the perfection of heavenly life, seeking not earthly things but heavenly things.

entries.section: (1) The future of the Jews with regard to salvation

paragraphs.text: Likewise in the time of Paul, indeed in all times, there is a chosen Israelite remnant who enter into faith in Christ. How does this happen? By the election of grace, that is, God looks upon hearts and sees who is ready to receive Him, and sends him the grace of the Holy Spirit to support him, enlighten his heart and strengthen him to enter the Christian faith and be baptized, so that the Holy Spirit abides in him forever.

entries.section: (1) The future of the Jews with regard to salvation

paragraphs.text: "No more of works": that is, the works of the Law.
"Otherwise grace is no more grace": grace would be of no benefit for salvation.
"But if it be of works, then is it no more grace": if salvation were by the works of the Law, it would not be by the grace of Christ, and the works of the Law would suffice us for salvation.

"Otherwise work is no more work": the works of the Law would no longer be a work that saves man, but rather a preparation for rejecting sin, so that we may believe in Christ and receive salvation by His grace.

St. Paul returns to affirm that their election is not based on the works of their law. For if their works were the cause of their salvation, they would have no need of the grace of God. And who can be saved without the grace of God?

entries.section: (1) The future of the Jews with regard to salvation

paragraphs.text: Israel did not obtain salvation because it sought it, as though it were an absolute right that it deserved because it had worked by the Law. The elect among the Israelites obtained salvation through their humility and their reliance on the grace of Christ, but the rest, the proud and hard of heart, who rejected the despised, crucified Christ, did not obtain salvation.

entries.section: (1) The future of the Jews with regard to salvation

paragraphs.text: When God found them hard of heart, He left them in their hardness and withheld His grace from them because they rejected it. When a person looks at them, he finds them as though in a deep sleep, neither hearing nor seeing. Behold, the world around them believes in Christ and receives salvation in every generation. Although they saw Christ and heard His teaching, they closed their hearts, eyes and ears to Him. This verse is a prophecy about them from both Moses the prophet (Deut 29:4) and Isaiah the prophet (Isa 29:10-12).

entries.section: (1) The future of the Jews with regard to salvation

paragraphs.text: This verse is also a prophecy about them from David the prophet. The table signifies the Law, on which the Jews relied and with which alone they were satisfied, while rejecting Christ. This same Law will judge them, that is, it will be a snare and a ruin to them on the day of judgment. Thus St. Paul has called the prophets of the Jews, Moses, Isaiah and David, to witness against them in their rejection of faith in Christ.

entries.section: (1) The future of the Jews with regard to salvation

paragraphs.text: That verse, from Ps 69:22-23, does not mean that the Apostle Paul is invoking blindness and a bowed back upon them. Rather, he wants to say that whoever wants blindness and a bowed back, that is, incapacity for spiritual work in spite of God's calling him, let it be to him as he wishes. The grace of God will no longer press upon him, but God will leave him, so that when he is wearied he may return to God and repent.

Note, beloved, that the table of the Old Testament is very rich, for it contains many symbols of the atoning work of Christ, but the Jews, sadly, took the words of the Law literally and did not understand that it is a symbol and a preparation for Christ.

Be ready at all times to learn from those around you, and do not let pride prevent you from being a disciple and from understanding God's messages to you on the lips of those around you. For humility is the way to knowledge, wisdom and all that is good.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: "Stumbled": they did not believe, trust and accept Christ the Savior.
"Fall": that God rejected them to the end.
"To provoke them to jealousy": that is, so that they may become zealous and turn to faith in Christ.
St. Paul asks a rhetorical question: does the Jews' unbelief that Jesus is the awaited Messiah, and their rejection of Him, mean that they have fallen utterly?

Certainly not, for their stumbling is a temporary period, so that when they turned away from faith, God turned to rescue the Gentiles. One of the benefits of this, perhaps, is to stir up a spirit of jealousy in the hearts of the Jews.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: "Their fall": a temporary fall through their rejection of faith in Christ and His crucifixion.
"Their diminishing": their being empty of faith in Christ.
St. Paul returns to lift the spirits of the Jews, so he describes their condition as a "fall," just as he showed that God turned their fall to good by opening His arms to the Gentiles.

But the greatest joy will be at their fullness, that is, the return of the majority of them to faith in Christ, which will be a blessing for the whole world, for the material world will end and we will begin to enjoy the Kingdom of Heaven, and that will be at the end of the days.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: Here he reassures the Gentiles that he was not distracted from them by serving the Jews, affirming that he is essentially an apostle to the Gentiles, and that this ministry must be glorified and bear more and more fruit.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: Paul speaks in this manner in the hope that it may lead the Jews to be jealous of the glory that the Gentiles have received, and so believe.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: When the Jews rejected the Lord Christ, the pagan half entered into faith. Therefore when the Jewish half returns to faith in Christ, the world, in both its Jewish and Gentile halves, will be in the faith; that is, the whole world will be raised from the death of sin and denial, enjoying the spiritual resurrection and in a state of reconciliation with God.
In sum, the Jews will return to the faith before the end of the world, and God awaits their return.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: Now, what is the value of the Jews in God's sight? Here St. Paul likens the Fathers (Abraham, Isaac and Jacob) to the firstfruit (which is the offering of the first of the harvest to God, so that the whole wheat crop used for the dough is blessed by it), and likens the Jewish people to the holy lump itself. Then he returns to liken the Fathers to the root (the root and trunk of a good tree) and the Jewish people to the good branches of that tree.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: But some dry branches came out of that tree, that is, the Jews who refused to believe, so God cut them off and cast them away. And you, O Gentile, are like a wild olive tree (which bears no fruit); God had compassion on you in His mercy and found in you a readiness to partake with the rich olive tree, so He grafted you into it, and you have become related to it and nourished by it.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: Certainly you cannot boast against the broken-off branches, that is, the Jews who were rejected for their unbelief, thinking that you are better, even if you bear beautiful spiritual fruit. The glory, the boast and the credit go back to the root, that is, the fathers and prophets of the Jewish people, which bears you and nourishes you, and without which you would have fallen.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: If you say in your heart, "I am the branch that stands, better than the original branches that were broken off, because God rejected them and put me in their place," then know the true reason for their fall, which is unbelief, and the true reason for your standing, which is your faith. This makes you not proud and boastful, but fearful of falling.

The fear of God is the way of your salvation, and your humility supports you. So examine yourself with repentance, knowing that you are less than all creatures, yet it is God who glorifies you with His love and His gifts. The more you fear God, the more you reject sin, so your heart is purified, you cling to His love, and you live for Him with all your heart.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: For God's rule is that the unbeliever is cut off. If this rule applies without partiality to the natural branches, that is, the Jews who rejected Christ, what then of the grafted branches that are not original, that is, the Gentiles, if they do not abide in faith? Without doubt, if they reject faith they will perish.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: God is kind to those who abide in faith, but He is severe and cuts off those who reject faith, who do not abide in it and who despise His kindness.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: As for the natural branches that were cut off, that is, the Jews who rejected faith, God will graft them in again if they leave the state of unbelief in which they are, for God is able to draw them to faith.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: Paul declares that the faith and return of the Jews who rejected it is not impossible, for if you, O Gentile, a wild olive tree different from the original olive tree, were grafted into it by God, how much more easily can God graft in the branches that have the same nature as the original olive tree, that is, the Jews when they repent.

For this reason the Church loved the books of the Old Testament and read them, and even took chapters from them for her Church readings, because it is the root of the olive tree. She looks to the Jews to return to the olive tree and come back to faith, since apart from faith they are like a dry, dead branch whose end is fire. The Lord Christ said to every person in (Jn 15:6), "If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned."

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: Here St. Paul sums up the truth that every Gentile must not forget: that Israel has been hardened in part, that is, some of the Jews rejected faith so that an opportunity might be given to the Gentiles to enter it. The Gentile should not think that the story ended at this point, lest he be ignorant of the wisdom of God, who will receive the Jews into the faith before the end of the days. This is a clear prophecy of the faith of the Jews at the end of the days. St. Paul called this event a mystery, because it is hard for the human mind to grasp that the Jews who crucified Christ will return to believe in Him after all these long years of denial.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: How will Israel be saved? By the Deliverer, Jesus Christ, who works in hearts and changes them when they show readiness for that, and turns them away from their evils. And what is the greatest ungodliness? Is it not the denial of Christ?

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: In sum, God promises the return of Israel to the faith at the end of the days, when they leave their sins, that is, the hardness of their hearts, their rejection of Christ and all their evil desires.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: The Jews are now considered enemies of the Gospel and of the preaching of it, until the preaching reaches the whole world. The Americas, for example, did not receive the preaching until the sixteenth century, and Africa in the twentieth century. Until faith reaches all the nations, that is, the fullness of the Gentiles (v. 25), the Jews will remain enemies of the Gospel. Then the Jews will return to faith because they are originally God's chosen people, and beloved of God for the sake of their fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: These are the fathers to whom God promised that their descendants would remain His people, and God cannot go back on His promises and gifts.

The Jews have misunderstood these verses of St. Paul's epistle, and thought that he was prophesying to them the establishment of a state that usurps the rights of others in order to restore its former glory and revive its religion with its sacrifices and its temple. Of course St. Paul did not mean this, because Christianity does not tie believers to an earthly inheritance but to a heavenly kingdom that does not perish.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: And you, O Gentiles, God called you from the beginning of humanity, but you rejected God's call while Abraham and his people accepted it. But now, after your repentance, you have become worthy of mercy, while the Jews disobeyed. But when the Jews repent and return to God at the end of the days, they will be shown mercy with the same kind of mercy that you were shown.
Perhaps these verses are a lesson to every person not to despise anyone, however great his sin. For who knows, perhaps that sinner today will be a great saint tomorrow.

entries.section: (2) God's call to the Jews to believe in Christ

paragraphs.text: For God first closed the door of mercy on the Gentiles because of their earlier disobedience to Christ, and then closed the door of mercy on the Jews because of their disobedience after the Incarnation of Christ. Then the door of mercy was opened to the Gentiles after they accepted Christ from the first century, and the door of mercy will be opened to the Jews before the Second Coming of Christ. So all, Gentiles and Jews, are equal in that they were rejected once and shown mercy once. Thus the mercy of Christ will come upon all, though at different times.

entries.section: (3) The loftiness of God's wisdom

paragraphs.text: Truly, what a wondrous composition and what a wisdom beyond comprehension belongs to God! He directs all events so that they achieve their noble aims in the end. And what a great foreknowledge He has! Who can claim knowledge and say, "I can examine the judgments of God," as though he were greater than God, or who can investigate and search out God's ways and methods, as though God's plans lacked precision or wisdom?

entries.section: (3) The loftiness of God's wisdom

paragraphs.text: Who can say, "I know how God thinks," or "I am God's counselor"?

entries.section: (3) The loftiness of God's wisdom

paragraphs.text: Who gave God something of his own, as a man, and so deserved a reward for his gift to God? That is, what did Israel give God that it dares to demand its right, as though God were indebted to it?

entries.section: (3) The loftiness of God's wisdom

paragraphs.text: "For of him" (God created all things), "and through him" (all things exist, live, are preserved and remain by His power and wisdom), "and to him" (all things are indebted to Him and work for His glory). In sum, God deserves all glory.

Finally, beloved, things may happen in your life that seem hard to understand and that the human mind cannot grasp now, but the great wisdom of God, which keeps and shepherds you, will be revealed to you one day, and then you will realize how much God loved you, and that all His plans and arrangements turned out for your good in the end, because He alone is the Maker of good things, the merciful and compassionate. So accept all that comes upon you and thank God for it, confident of His love and His fatherhood toward you.
Gifts and virtues, from chapter 12 to 16: the practical commandments in the Epistle to the Romans

entries.section: (1) Sanctifying the body and the mind for the spiritual life with God

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Paul directs the attention of the believers to the fact that, since God has dealt with them with all compassion, offering them salvation and redemption, they must in return, in order to keep these abundant blessings, present all their members to do good, righteousness and holiness, slay and drive out every evil desire that opposes this, and let the mind take part in praising and worshiping God.

entries.section: (1) Sanctifying the body and the mind for the spiritual life with God

paragraphs.text: The believer ought not to be conformed to the people of the world. How many behaviors or habits the world offers that contradict the commandment of Christ, and it even dares to accuse the Church and her children of being closed-minded and reactionary. Therefore we must not keep pace with the people of the world or please them, but let our minds and thoughts be enlightened every day by the thoughts of the Holy Bible, so that we may go from depth to depth in the spiritual life and become nearer to and more understanding of God's good will in our lives, and this is reflected in our outward conduct ("your form").

Know that you live in the world, but your principles are different from it. So do not share in its errors, and if you have been drawn along with it in some improper behaviors, you need repentance and the renewing of your mind, so that you may live for the love of God. Be strong in cutting off sin and everything that leads you to it, so that you may live occupied with the love of God.

entries.section: (2) The kinds of gifts in the Church

paragraphs.text: St. Paul begins to explain the manner of service and the kinds of gifts in the Church, not as one speaking from himself, but under the guidance of the Holy Spirit within him.
May the servant always speak after praying to consult God, and not rush into speaking, relying on his own knowledge.

Then St. Paul says that the believer ought not to "think of himself more highly than he ought to think," that is, not to see himself, in conceit, as having great abilities beyond what is true, but to see himself as he truly is, so that he may recognize what gift God has given him and work with it in faith. For the work of service is built essentially on trust in the work of God, however weak a person's abilities may be.

entries.section: (2) The kinds of gifts in the Church

paragraphs.text: Our God is a God of order. He made the members of His Church like the members of one body, each one having a specific role and a specific function different from the other's yet complementing it. The gifts given to each member of the Church are meant to serve others, not for personal boasting.

entries.section: (2) The kinds of gifts in the Church

paragraphs.text: The grace of the Holy Spirit determines, with great wisdom, for each person the gift he will receive according to his personal readiness to receive it. The gifts are not divided into great kinds and small kinds, because the Church needs all the gifts with the same importance, so no one should look at his brother's gift and covet it. These gifts are:

First, prophecy: it is the revealing of heavenly mysteries and future events, and among the most famous of these prophecies is the Book of Revelation of St. John the Beloved. The Holy Spirit gives this gift if He finds faith in the speaker and the listener.

In the New Testament, the future is the Kingdom of Heaven, so speaking about it, that is, about our relationship with God and how He reigns over our lives in preparation for eternity, is another meaning of prophecy.

entries.section: (2) The kinds of gifts in the Church

paragraphs.text: Second, ministry: this differs from social services in that it essentially has a lofty goal, which is to bring the one served to the Lord Christ.
Third, teaching: this is different from prophesying, for it is the explanation and simplification of the truths of faith and theological matters so that the simple person served may understand them.
